title: The Hydrogen Stream: Dutch researchers calculate green H2 costs as low as €7.2/kg
content:
Researchers at the University of Groningen have calculated green hydrogen production costs of €7.2/kg to €7.3/kg using renewable power purchase agreements and hybrid electricity supply configurations, compared with €7.7/kg for wholesale electricity sourcing. The study found that long-term revenue guarantees are essential to making large-scale hydrogen projects financially viable.

title: Prices drive Pakistan’s metered solar, outages drive hidden uptake
content:
A new study finds that Pakistan's net-metering capacity is concentrated in the best-served, higher-income utility areas, while much of the country's solar sits unregistered, off-grid and behind the meter where outages are worst.

title: Isaias ends historic Atlantic hurricane lull after sunny southern summer
content:
In a new weekly update for pv magazine, Solcast, a DNV company, reports that an unusually quiet Atlantic hurricane season brought 10–20% above-average solar irradiance to Mexico and the southern US in August–September, while prolonged dry weather increased solar panel soiling losses. Tropical Storm Isaias is set to end the sunny spell, bringing widespread cloud cover, reduced irradiance, and potential hurricane impacts along the US Gulf Coast.

title: Spanish researchers reduce losses in organic solar cells by restricting emission angle
content:
Spanish researchers have developed an optical cavity that reduces Boltzmann losses in organic solar cells by restricting photon emission angles. The approach could help push single-junction solar cell efficiencies beyond the Shockley-Queisser limit.

title: European storage inventories on the rise
content:
In an interview with pv magazine, Ali Arfa, analyst at EUPD Research, said China’s dominance of the global battery supply chain is unlikely to change significantly over the next two years. He expects rising inventories to put pressure on residential and C&I storage prices in Europe, while utility-scale battery prices should remain broadly stable.

title: Plug-in PV is growing – are regulations keeping pace?
content:
Plug-in solar PV and compact battery storage are expanding access to solar energy, but differing national regulations raise challenges around electrical safety, certification and consumer protection. IEA PVPS will host two free online seminars on 19 and 28 October 2026 to compare international approaches and promote the safe deployment of these technologies.

title: PowerChina switches on 1 GW PV-CSP hybrid plant in northwestern China
content:
PowerChina has completed grid connection of a 1 GW hybrid solar project in Qinghai province, China. The facility combines 900 MW of solar PV capacity with a 100 MW concentrated solar power (CSP) plant featuring eight hours of molten-salt thermal storage and a 20 MW electric heater to store surplus PV electricity.

title: IEA: Thermal energy storage key to industrial heat electrification that could cut EU gas demand by 35 bcm annually
content: Electrifying low-temperature industrial heat and steam processes with renewables could reduce European Union natural gas consumption by 35 billion cubic metres-per-year, according to a report from the International Energy Agency (IEA).
